title: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training for Natural Language Generation, Translation, and Comprehension
summary:
we present BART , a denoising autoencoder for pretraining sequence-to-sequence models . 
 BART is trained by ( 1 ) corrupting text with an arbitrary noising function , and ( 2 ) learning a sequence- to-sequence model to reconstruct the original text . it uses a standard tranformer-based neural machine translationarchitecture which , despite its sim-
plicity , can be seen as generalizing bERT ( due to the bidirectional encoder ) , gPT ( with the left-to - right decoder ) and many other more re-cent pretraining schemes . a key advantage of this setup is the noisingexibil-
ity ; arbitrary transformations can be applied to the orig-inal text , including changing its length . we evaluate a number of noising approaches , ﬁnding the best per-formance by both randomly shufﬂing the or-
der of the original sentences and using a novel in-ﬁlling scheme , where spans of text are re-placed with a single mask token . this ap-
proach generalizes the original word masking and nextsentence prediction objectives in bERT by forcing themodel to reason more about
key_findings: BART is a denoising autoencoder for pretraining sequence-to-sequence models.
The model is trained by corrupting text and learning to reconstruct the original text.
BART generalizes existing pretraining schemes like BERT and GPT.
The best performance is achieved by shuffling sentence order and using a novel in-filling scheme.
methodology: BART employs a transformer-based architecture, training on corrupted text to reconstruct the original sequences.
limitations: The effectiveness of BART may vary with different noising functions.
The model's performance is dependent on the quality of the training data.
Limited exploration of noising methods beyond those evaluated.
future_work: Investigate additional noising functions for improved performance.
Explore the application of BART in other natural language processing tasks.
Enhance the model's robustness against various types of text corruption.
